root_idea.summary: An unsuspected taking or seizure: something removes or destroys a person or thing from an unperceived quarter.
root_idea.development: The root develops from covert seizure into destruction, disappearance, misleading distance, harmful consequences, ghoulish beings, and concealed instruments of attack.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Classical Arabic noun غَوْل.

senses.definition: A harmful or insidious effect or consequence; in the wine of Paradise, no intoxicating, headache-producing, mind-clouding, or distressing aftereffect is present.
senses.usage_conditions: Used in لَا فِيهَا غَوْلٌ to deny the adverse effects associated with intoxicating wine, including headache, intoxication, loss of reason, and related distress or molestation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To destroy, seize, or carry away unexpectedly; said of a cause, death, or a tract of land that causes people to perish or go astray.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object may be a person or thing, and the taking may occur from an unknown quarter or without the person's awareness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To corrupt, impair, or destroy; of wine, to deprive someone of reason or bodily soundness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative use in which a substance or other agent produces impairment or ruin.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To exceed the measure of clothing so that it falls short.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A construction used of a tall woman whose garments are too short for her.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To withhold or debar someone from coming.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the expression مَا غَالَكَ عَنَّا.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To steal something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical variant also recorded under the related form غِيلَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a desert, to make its roads unapparent and cause its travelers to go astray.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a waterless or trackless desert whose routes are difficult to discern.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hastening, striving to be first, or trying to accomplish or obtain something before others.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May apply to journeying or to competing in action.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To change or vary in state, form, or appearance; to become altered, dubious, or confused.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a person, a desert, or an affair; a person may be described as assuming a ghoul-like appearance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A ghoul or destructive demon-like being; by extension, anything that unexpectedly destroys a person or causes the intellect to depart.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Traditional descriptions include a being appearing in various forms, misleading travelers, and destroying them; the lexical entry also records male jinn usage and related senses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To hasten together, vie with one another, or strive to be beforehand.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal construction describing competition in speed or in making a sudden attack.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To kill covertly or when the victim is unaware.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form VIII verb synonymous with قتلَ in this use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To deprive of strength or vehemence through satiety.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative expression said of a hawk whose energy and force of flight are not diminished by having eaten its fill.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of land, to make the footing or course of travelers unapparent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The obscuring is attributed to the land's great extent and breadth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To overtake someone in running.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A meaning reported in an additional lexical citation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fill something until the available space becomes too narrow to contain it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported extended meaning; the attestation is attributed to an additional lexical source.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The far extent of a desert or land, especially an expanse that causes travelers to disappear or perish.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in expressions describing land that appears small at a distance but extends very far.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Great height or exceptional extension, including the height of a tall woman.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal expression such as ذَاتُ غَوْلٍ is used of a tall woman.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In a tentatively interpreted phrase, exceptional swiftness, said of a she-camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This meaning is restricted to the reported phrase نَاقَةُ غَوْلِ النَّجَاءِ and is uncertain in the source.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Unfaithfulness or unfaithful conduct.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical Arabic nominal use distinct from the Quranic sense of harmful aftereffect.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cunning or bad action.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the expression أَتَى غَوْلًا.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A large quantity or expanse of earth or sand.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in descriptions of extensive sand or land.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A distinctive collection of talh trees.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized botanical use describing a stand of trees with nothing else mixed among them.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A low or depressed part of the earth or land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A geographical nominal use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Destruction, death, the decree of death, or a calamity or misfortune.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct vocalized noun from غَوْل; it may denote either the destructive event or the misfortune resulting from it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A serpent, especially in a poetic description of its fangs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usage may be literal or an exaggeration, and some interpreters understand the poetic reference as meaning devils.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Covert or opportunistic slaying.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal noun from اِغْتَالَ, originally preserving the root vowel represented by و.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A slender pasture plant of the ḥamḍ kind, compared with kali or glasswort.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A botanical noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The singular of غَوَالِينُ, the ribs or rib-like structural members of a ship or boat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nautical use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Destructive or engulfing, especially of land that destroys its inhabitant through its great extent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An active-participle adjective applied to land.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Caused to disappear, hidden, concealed, or stolen.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A feminine adjectival use describing something made absent or removed from view.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Bad or corrupt conduct, evil, mischief, or a harmful consequence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used in the expression أَخَافُ غَائِلَتَهُ, ‘I fear its harmful result.’

other_classical_meanings.definition: Wickedness, disobedience, or running away, especially of a slave.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized legal and social use; its plural in this sense is غَوَائِلُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A third party's right to a slave that voids the sale and obliges the seller to return the price.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized defect affecting the validity of a slave sale.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Places of destruction.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural use of غَائِلَة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A hole or perforation in a watering-trough or tank through which the water escapes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized term for a defect that causes stored water to pass away.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A far-extending tract of land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A descriptive use applied to land.

other_classical_meanings.definition: More or most destructive.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A comparative or superlative adjective, including the figurative comparison of anger with other destroyers.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Soft, plentiful, and easy living.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression عَيْشٌ أَغْوَلُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A concealed knife, slender sword, or similar iron weapon used to destroy or kill unexpectedly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The weapon may be hidden within or sheathed by a whip, or worn concealed beneath clothing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A quality of outstripping or surpassing, said of a mare that leaves other horses behind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative adjectival construction based on the weapon's destructive effect.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having gone far in journeying.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the phrase نَزَلُوا مُغَاوِلِينَ, describing travelers who alighted after a long journey.

cautions: The Quranic noun is غَوْل, meaning a harmful effect; it should not be conflated by vocalization with غُول, the classical ghoul or demon.
The Quranic lexical sense groups closely related traditional explanations—headache, intoxication, loss of reason, and distress—as manifestations of one denied harmful aftereffect.
The interpretation of نَاقَةُ غَوْلِ النَّجَاءِ as referring to exceptional swiftness is tentative.
